channel.description: Latest articles from The Garden Island (thegardenisland.com)

item.title: Presidents’ Day notice to our readers
item.description: LIHUE — The Monday, Feb. 16, edition of The Garden Island will not be delivered via mail because the U.S. Postal Service will be closed in observance of the Presidents’ Day holiday.

item.title: Happy Camper for Monday, February 16, 2026
item.description: Shauncey Nakano of The Craft Bar (Maile Maglinti and Kelly Rapozo were on a food finding mission on Friday night) was “Sipping and Sliming” with the Little Babes Club on Friday. The Craft Bar had drinks (non-alcoholic, and some are Sprite-based) for purchase in the collaboration that covered the opening day of the Kauai Quilt Show Quilt Parade on Friday, and overflowed to the Hearts and Horses (Valentine’s Day, Chinese New Year) campaign on Saturday.

item.title: Hawai‘i Pacific Health, HMSA partnership plans proceeding
item.description: Two dominant players in Hawaii’s health care landscape continue to press forward on their plans to form a partnership.

item.title: Loyola masters challenging conditions at Burns Intercollegiate
item.description: NAWILIWILI — Despite the strong trade winds that buffeted the island on Saturday, Trevor Algya of Loyola Marymount enjoyed his best day of the 3-day John A. Burns Intercollegiate golf tournament at the Ocean Course Hokuala.

item.title: Hawaii legislative bills aim to rewrite crosswalk safeguards
item.description: Out on Kapahulu Avenue last week, pedestrian after pedestrian who waited at crosswalks to get to the other side welcomed a pair of bills moving through the state Legislature that would require drivers on all islands to wait even longer.

item.title: Monks walked for 4 months. Here’s what people learned from them.
item.description: TRIANGLE, Va. — The roads were slick with ice, the ground was caked with hardened snow, and the stiff winds made an already brutally cold day in the Virginia suburbs feel below zero. Yet people came out by the hundreds.

item.title: Bill seeks study of child welfare court processes
item.description: A bill to fund a study to improve family court processes, including providing youths in the child welfare system access to legal representation, unanimously passed first reading at the state Legislature.

item.title: Able Prom celebrated at the Royal Sonesta
item.description: NAWILIWILI — When doors to the Royal Sonesta Kauai Resort opened on Feb. 7 for the Kauai Able Prom, there were more than 100 guests welcomed in “true red-carpet style,” said Ana Munoz, an Able Ministries volunteer and coordinator of the 12th annual event.

item.title: U.S. Archbishop will be beatified, one step away from sainthood
item.description: The Vatican will allow an American archbishop, who was one of the best-known Catholic clergy of the last century, to be beatified, ending a six-year delay and placing him one step away from sainthood.
